title: Synthetic US tax provision, filing, withholding, and tax-family boundary fixture
summary: Original synthetic scenarios for a US corporate book-to-tax bridge, separate return and withholding populations, a method-change evidence route, cross-border missing-document handling, and the boundary to sales/use/payroll taxes.
jurisdiction: United States federal tax; selected Texas sales/use context; synthetic only

editorial_review.reviewer: Codex AI-assisted original-source and synthetic-fixture review
editorial_review.basis: Arithmetic and evidence-routing branches were checked against the issue package and linked source records. No taxpayer evidence, professional review, or external operational validation was used.

data.scope: All amounts, entities, invoices, certificates, rates, classifications, and dates below are synthetic assumptions. They illustrate retrieval and control boundaries only.
inputs: Declare tax year, entity and recipient roles, accounting basis, payment character, source cutoff, and tax family.
Preserve unavailable treaty, entity, certificate, rate, classification, and effective-date facts as unresolved rather than filling them in.
Use source records for routing and citations; do not treat a synthetic event as evidence of a real filing or tax result.

examples.title: Declared-assumption federal book-to-tax bridge

facts.accounting_basis: US GAAP context, with authoritative Topic 740 text unavailable in this packet

calculation: Hypothetical temporary-difference balance from the depreciation assumption = 20000 * r.
No real tax rate, permanent classification, depreciation method, deferred-tax recognition, or uncertain-position conclusion is asserted.
controls: Tie every adjustment to a dated evidence row and label it assumed, evidenced, or unresolved.
Review current tax, deferred tax, rate reconciliation, and tax-return populations separately.
Do not replace the symbolic rate with a default percentage.
unavailable_facts: Enacted rate and jurisdictional rate stack
Actual depreciation methods, placed-in-service dates, and tax basis
ASC Topic 740 authoritative text and professional provision review
State, local, foreign, uncertain-position, and valuation-allowance facts

examples.title: Separate Form 1120 and Form 1042-S populations

facts.corporate_return: Synthetic corporation's annual Form 1120 population for the declared tax year
facts.withholding_agent_return: Synthetic payer's Form 1042 and Form 1042-S population for foreign-person payments
facts.recipient_certificate: Synthetic W-8BEN-E is present in one branch and expired or missing in another

workflow: Do not merge the corporation's income-tax return population with the withholding agent's foreign-payee population.
For the withholding population, reconcile payment rows to Form 1042-S records, then reconcile Form 1042-S totals to Form 1042.
If the certificate is missing or expired, record the presumption branch and obtain human review; do not infer a percentage.
unavailable_facts: Payment character, source, treaty claim, beneficial ownership, and rate
E-file configuration, transmission evidence, and correction event

examples.title: Two otherwise similar invoices with different evidence

invoices.place_of_performance: All services performed outside the United States in the assumed branch
invoices.certificate: Current certificate supplied in the assumed branch
invoices.route: Evidence review required; no withholding result or rate is concluded.

invoices.character: Same nominal service label, but contract and work log show performance in the United States in the assumed branch
invoices.place_of_performance: United States in the assumed branch
invoices.certificate: Certificate expired or missing in the assumed branch
invoices.route: Different source and documentation branch; presumption and human review required.

controls: Compare contract, invoice, work log, location, recipient, certificate, and payment-date evidence.
Do not use the invoice label alone to decide source or withholding.
Do not use a universal withholding percentage.
unavailable_facts: Beneficial ownership and effectively connected income analysis

examples.title: Method-change routing and section 481(a) bridge

facts.section_481_adjustment: Not calculated because the affected-item schedule is unavailable

workflow: Identify the item and Code section, then obtain the current requested-year revenue procedure and Form 3115 instructions.
Determine automatic or non-automatic routing only after eligibility facts are checked.
Reconcile old method, proposed method, cumulative difference, inclusion period, prior returns, and exceptions before any filing decision.
unavailable_facts: Current automatic-change list and taxpayer eligibility
Current Form 3115 successor instructions and professional review

examples.title: Federal income-tax boundary to sales/use and payroll tax

facts.federal_income_tax: Synthetic Form 1120 and book-to-tax bridge population
facts.sales_use_tax: Synthetic Texas contract and destination facts required; no rate or exemption supplied
facts.payroll_tax: Synthetic employer and worker population required; no payroll rate or state rule supplied

workflow: Stop and classify the tax family when a prompt changes from federal income tax to sales/use or payroll tax.
For sales/use tax, request item, contract, seller, delivery destination, exemption, permit, and nexus facts.
For payroll tax, request employer, worker, period, withholding, deposit, reporting, and jurisdiction facts.
unavailable_facts: Current rates, registrations, exemptions, and professional review

limitations: Synthetic example: no real taxpayer, invoice, certificate, return, workpaper, or filing is represented.
The arithmetic is illustrative and uses a symbolic rate and assumed classifications.
No professional review, licensed Topic 740 review, treaty analysis, rate determination, filing, or empirical agent validation was performed.
